subject: Exec review: liability cap & warranty changes requested by QuantumBioMed
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exec review: QuantumBioMed requested changes — liability/warranty/discount (attachments)

Hi team,

Following up from today's call with QuantumBioMed (Elena + procurement). They're asking for three non-standard items before advancing procurement:

1) Liability cap increase to $5,000,000 aggregate (Redwood standard is $1,000,000).
2) Broader indemnity language to explicitly cover IP-related claims and a narrower carve-out for data-related claims (they want mutual IP indemnity).
3) Warranty window extended to 90 days (we usually do 30 days for software defects) plus a request for a 12-month SLA credit schedule tied to uptime.

They've also pushed for a 35% discount off list pricing for a 36-month term and want the attached SOW included in the contract. I attached their redlines (Redlines_20271029.pdf) and the current SOW (SOW_QBM_v3.docx).

Quick context: QBM is a late-stage medtech company, POC is complete and they want to go-live with our Dedicated offering. Estimated first-year spend ~ $1.2M ARR. Procurement is escalating timing pressure — they want a signed agreement by mid-December to hit their budget cycle.

Ask: please advise what requires exec sign-off and what legal can accept as counter-proposals. If this needs an explicit exec authorization memo, I can draft a one-pager with contract value/risk mitigations for Aditya.

Attachments: Redlines_20271029.pdf, SOW_QBM_v3.docx

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Exec review: QuantumBioMed requested changes — liability/warranty/discount (attachments)

Marcus — thanks for the summary and attachments. Have reviewed the redlines at a high level. A few immediate legal concerns and clarification requests: 

- Liability cap: $5M is materially above our standard. We can consider a higher cap if tied to objective limits (e.g., capped at greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $X) or if the customer provides acceptable insurance (cyber liability + tech E&O). Please confirm the customer's willingness to provide a certificate naming Redwood.

- Indemnity: expanding IP indemnity to be mutual is common, but the proposed language as written is very broad (no limitation on third-party claims, no requirement to mitigate). We should narrow to third-party IP claims that arise from use of the service and include obligations to provide notice and allow Redwood to control defense. Also add a reasonableness requirement for indemnity caps.

- Warranty: 90 days is acceptable in principle for defect remediation, but SLA credits tied to uptime need clear definitions (measurement windows, credit caps, remedy waterfall). Do *not* agree to a warranty that covers integrations or third-party data; add explicit carve-outs.

Proposed path: legal can prepare a compromise redline that (a) increases cap to a fixed multiple tied to fees (e.g., 3x annual fees) but not exceeding $3.5M without exec sign-off; (b) refines IP indemnity language with standard Redwood controls; (c) accept 90-day warranty limited to Redwood service defects and with defined SLA credit table.

I'll draft suggested language and attach a short memo documenting risk and mitigations. Need confirmation on the customer's insurance position and whether they will accept an aggregate cap tied to fees.

Looping back with additional customer context so legal and execs can assess tradeoffs.

- Business value: QBM sees Redwood as a strategic inference platform for their drug-safety models. They expect to expand to other teams if initial deployment succeeds. First-year spend ~ $1.2M; 3-yr committed ARR with 35% concession would still be a meaningful contract for Redwood.

- Procurement pressure: they must present a vendor contract to their finance committee in early December. The procurement lead (Elena) indicated they will push for $5M cap as a showstopper — their counsel expects a higher cap for platforms hosting regulated workloads.

- Risk mitigations QBM accepts: add SOC 2 + pen test results, allow customer-controlled VPC for Dedicated, and a requirement that Redwood carry cyber liability insurance naming them as additional insured. They are open to tying cap to whether we host customer data or not.

Request to the team: if an exec exception is needed, please indicate the minimum approvals required (VP Sales, CRO, CEO) and any conditional language that would change the cap/indemnity outcome. I attached the current SOW for reference (SOW_QBM_v3.docx).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if useful.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Director, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Exec review: QuantumBioMed requested changes — liability/warranty/discount (attachments)

Thanks for the clear thread and the proposed legal path. I reviewed the customer context and legal's preliminary guidance. Decision and required conditions below.

Executive decision (approved with conditions):
1) Liability cap: approve exception up to $3,500,000 aggregate (not $5M). Any cap > $3.5M requires CEO sign-off. The cap must be expressed as aggregate liability and exclude amounts recoverable under commercial insurance.

2) Indemnity: legal to accept mutual IP indemnity limited to third-party claims that arise from use of the Service. Redwood must retain the right to control defense; mutual indemnity must include a reasonableness and mitigation obligation. No open-ended open-source or statutory liabilities.

3) Warranty: accept 90-day defect warranty limited to Redwood-owned service code and infrastructure. Explicit carve-outs for integrations, customer-supplied data, and third-party services. SLA credits may be included but credit cap cannot exceed 25% of monthly service fees in a single quarter.

4) Insurance/mitigations required before signing: customer must provide cyber liability or tech E&O insurance certificate (minimum $10M); accept periodic pen test / SOC2 reports; enable customer-controlled VPC for Dedicated deployment as specified in the SOW.

5) Commercial: authorize the 35% discount for a signed 36-month commitment only if contract signed by 2027-12-15 and SOW scope is locked (no add-on modules beyond defined scope without separate pricing). Finance must confirm revenue recognition impact; Rishi, please prepare a short approval note.

Laura — please update the redline reflecting the approved conditions and produce a one-page exec memo summarizing residual risk and the business justification. Marcus/Marissa — once legal delivers the compromise redline, loop in Elena for final confirmation.

Aditya Rao
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
